brief.motion: Cinematic and decisive: expo.inOut camera moves, back.out pops with small overshoot, a slow continuous drift so no frame is static, light sweeps and dust in a projector beam. Every key visual lands on the word that names it.
brief.story: Before and after, escalating: a plain white slide is directed into a dark film set (teal and amber grade, like a film), then each scene adds a new craft: story, layered redesign, 3D data, and the Pro offer, ending under the same beam it opened with.

scenes.narration: This is an ordinary slide. Watch it get directed, like the opening shot of a film.
scenes.storyboard: The real default title slide fills the frame in a plain editor window. On 'directed' a clapper-snap flash, then the slide breaks into a wave of tiles that tumble toward camera, revealing a dark stage with a projector beam and dust. The title is rebuilt as heavy kinetic type, letters rising through a mask, an amber light sweep crossing them.

scenes.storyboard: The five real slides fan in a 3D arc; an amber scan line reads across them on 'reads'. The deck's actual wordy speaker note is typeset below; on 'tightens' filler words are struck in ember and collapse out, the remaining words close up. On 'voiceover' the tightened line lifts and a waveform grows from it, a playhead sweeping across.

slide.title: How it works
slide.text: Reads the whole deck. Tightens the story. Speaker notes become the voiceover. Each slide becomes an animated scene
slide.notes: So basically how it works is the tool reads through all of the slides in the deck, and then it goes through and tightens up the story so it flows. The speaker notes that you have written get used as the voiceover. Then each slide gets redesigned as an animated scene, with the animation timed to the narration.
